articles.title: India Is 'Very, Very Close' to a Historic US Trade Deal — but a $500 Billion Target and New Tariffs Stand in the Way
articles.excerpt: As the India-UK CETA prepares to launch on July 15, Washington says a bilateral trade agreement with New Delhi is nearly done — while a proposed 12.5% forced-labour tariff threatens to complicate the final stretch
articles.image_caption: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds sign the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
articles.nri_angle: A US deal could lower tariff costs on Indian exports and ease barriers for IT professionals, while the UK CETA eliminates double social security payments for NRIs in Britain
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's SIP Investors Refuse to Blink — ₹30,000 Crore a Month Keeps Flowing Even as Equity Fund Inflows Drop 40%
articles.excerpt: Systematic investment plans held above ₹30,000 crore for three straight months through May 2026, absorbing a sharp lump-sum pullback and underlining a structural shift in how Indian retail money behaves.
articles.image_caption: The Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers, home of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who use SIP channels to invest in Indian mutual funds should note that the domestic retail floor is now structurally strong enough to cushion FII selling — a dynamic that reduces the kind of sharp drawdowns that used to punish long-distance investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Emerging as Asia's Safe Haven as the Global AI Selloff Crushes South Korea and Taiwan
articles.excerpt: With KOSPI plunging below 8,000 and foreigners dumping $137 billion of Asian equities in H1 2026, India's oil-fuelled rally and domestic-demand story are pulling global money in a new direction
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home of the Sensex
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with Asian market exposure face a historic rotation away from AI-heavy chip plays in Korea and Taiwan toward India, where oil collapse, rupee recovery, and domestic-demand sectors offer a compelling alternative.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Witness Its Biggest-Ever IPO Wave — From Jio's $3.8 Billion Listing to Carlsberg's Beer Play
articles.excerpt: Carlsberg has confidentially filed for a $700 million India IPO, joining a pipeline that includes Jio Platforms, NSE, PhonePe, and Pernod Ricard — collectively the largest collection of marquee listings India has ever seen in a single year
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, set to host what could be the country's biggest IPO wave
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who can access Indian IPOs through demat accounts or GIFT City–routed platforms face a once-in-a-generation lineup — but the sheer volume of issuance will test whether the market can absorb it all.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Households Just Sold 50 Tonnes of Gold in a Single Quarter — the Sharpest Spike in Years
articles.excerpt: Nearly 50 tonnes of old gold flooded back into the market in April–June 2026, a 43% jump from a year ago. For a nation that treats gold as heirloom, the shift from hoarding to liquidating signals something deeper than just falling prices.
articles.image_caption: Gold jewellery: Antique Indian Nose Ring Jewellery
articles.nri_angle: NRI families holding gold in India face rebalancing decisions as prices drop 22% from peak; the shift from physical hoarding to digital gold instruments reshapes how diaspora investors should think about gold in their Indian portfolio.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: KPIT Technologies Just Lost 17% in a Single Day — and 6 Lakh Retail Investors Are Caught in the Wreckage
articles.excerpt: The Pune-based auto software company's surprise profit warning, driven by sudden European OEM spending cuts, triggers JPMorgan downgrade and drags peers Tata Elxsi and LTTS down with it — a cautionary tale for NRI investors in India's mid-cap IT story
articles.image_caption: A stock trading screen showing market data — KPIT Technologies shares crashed 17% to a near four-year low on July 1, 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian mid-cap IT mutual funds are directly affected — KPIT's crash reveals the concentration risk in thematic auto-tech bets and raises questions about whether the broader Indian IT services sector faces structural headwinds from European demand weakness and AI disruption
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's GST Collections Just Surged 14% to ₹1.95 Lakh Crore — but Imports Are Doing the Heavy Lifting
articles.excerpt: June's headline growth looks robust, but a 34.6% surge in import revenues is masking modest 6.5% domestic growth. The divergence tells a nuanced story about where India's economy actually stands.
articles.image_caption: A government official addresses a GST Town Hall meeting in Bengaluru
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors should note the domestic GST growth of just 6.5% — well below the headline 14% — as a signal that India's consumption engine may need more time before justifying premium market valuations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Just Posted Its Steepest Quarterly Drop Since 2020 — and India May Be the Biggest Winner
articles.excerpt: Brent crude has crashed 43% from its Iran war peak to $71 a barrel, erasing the entire geopolitical risk premium. For the world's third-largest oil importer, the implications for inflation, the rupee, and the fiscal balance are enormous.
articles.image_caption: The Essar Oil Refinery in Gujarat — India imports nearly 90% of its crude, making it one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global oil price crash
articles.nri_angle: India imports 90% of its crude — the oil crash directly improves the current account, inflation outlook, rupee stability, and investment case that NRI portfolios depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Auto Giants Just Posted Blockbuster June Sales — Maruti Hit a Record 200K Units While Mahindra Surged 37%
articles.excerpt: The country's biggest carmakers reported their strongest June in years, led by an SUV boom and rising exports — but a historically dry monsoon and looming El Niño threaten the rural demand that sustains the volume story
articles.image_caption: A Maruti Suzuki car — the market leader sold a record 200,390 units in June 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indian auto stocks are among the most widely held by NRI investors — and the monsoon-versus-premiumization question will shape sector returns for the rest of FY27
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factory Growth Just Hit a Near Four-Year Low — and the Warning Signs Go Beyond One Bad Month
articles.excerpt: The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.2 in June as new orders, exports, and hiring all lost momentum — raising questions about whether the post-pandemic industrial boom is finally cooling.
articles.image_caption: Workers at a manufacturing facility in India — the country's factory sector expanded at its second-slowest pace in nearly four years (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian manufacturing, auto, and industrial stocks should monitor whether cooling factory demand translates into weaker corporate earnings in Q1 FY27 — and whether the RBI uses the data to justify another rate cut.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Had Its Fifth-Driest June Since 1901 — and the Monsoon Forecast for July Isn't Much Better
articles.excerpt: Rainfall in June was nearly 40% below average as El Niño conditions strengthened. Summer crop planting is down 23% year-on-year, and the weather department expects below-average rain through July. For NRI investors, the monsoon is now the single biggest variable for inflation, rural demand, and RBI rate policy in the second half of the year.
articles.image_caption: Indian farmland during monsoon season — summer crop planting is down 23% year-on-year after the driest June in over a decade
articles.nri_angle: The monsoon is now the single biggest variable for inflation, RBI rate policy, and rural consumption stocks in India — directly affecting NRI investment returns and the purchasing power of remittances sent home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Global Funds Are Quietly Returning to Indian Stocks — and the Data Shows the Tide May Finally Be Turning
articles.excerpt: Oil's 42% crash, a rupee rebound, and aggressive RBI reforms have eased the two biggest headwinds that drove $23 billion in foreign selling since 2025
articles.image_caption: Traders on the floor of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors evaluating re-entry into Indian equities face a macro backdrop that has improved dramatically — but monsoon deficits, U.S. rate risk, and sector rotation require selectivity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Banks Are the Healthiest in a Generation — and the RBI's New Stability Report Explains Why Investors Should Care
articles.excerpt: The June 2026 Financial Stability Report shows bank bad loans below 2%, credit growth at 14.5%, and stress-tested resilience — but also flags risks from state government debt and global AI-bubble fragilities that NRI investors should watch.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters building in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with bank deposits, mutual fund SIPs, and exposure to Indian financial stocks, the RBI's clean bill of health for the banking system is directly reassuring — but the risks flagged deserve equal attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Just Posted Its First Quarterly Gain Since March 2025 — Here's What Changed and What NRI Investors Should Watch Next
articles.excerpt: Oil's 42% crash from $126 to $73, a barrage of RBI measures, and $2.4 billion in net foreign inflows helped the rupee recover from record lows near 97 to settle around 94.66 — but the Fed's hawkish tilt and a weak monsoon cloud the outlook.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where Indian benchmarks posted monthly gains despite end-of-quarter jitters
articles.nri_angle: The rupee's recovery directly affects NRI remittances, SIP values, and NRE deposit returns — and the RBI's FCNR window at 7.5% offers a time-limited opportunity for diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Stocks Just Had Their Worst Month in Years — and the Threat Isn't Just Cyclical, It's Existential
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index fell 9.6% in June as Accenture's guidance cut, AI cannibalization fears, and Middle East demand shocks converged into a perfect storm for the $315 billion sector that employs millions of NRIs.
articles.image_caption: A stock exchange trading board displaying share prices in red and green, reflecting the market volatility that hit Indian IT stocks in June 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who work in IT services, hold IT stocks, or whose H-1B careers depend on the sector face employment risk, investment losses, and visa pipeline uncertainty as AI disruption and demand weakness converge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Just Poured a Record $3 Billion Into Indian Bonds in a Single Month — and the Biggest Catalyst Is Still Ahead
articles.excerpt: India's historic decision to scrap all taxes on foreign bond investments has triggered the largest monthly inflow ever under the Fully Accessible Route, with Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index inclusion now firmly on the horizon.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors holding or considering Indian government bonds stand to benefit from the tax exemptions and rising foreign demand, while RBI measures to boost dollar inflows are simultaneously improving FCNR deposit rates and rupee stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HDFC Bank Just Named a Former Election Chief and Banking Reformer as Its New Chairman — Here's What NRI Shareholders Should Know
articles.excerpt: The appointment of Rajiv Kumar, who once froze 3.38 lakh shell company accounts and led the merger of 27 public sector banks into 12, signals a governance reset at India's largest private lender after its previous chairman quit citing ethical concerns.
articles.image_caption: Rajiv Kumar, former Finance Secretary and Chief Election Commissioner, takes over as HDFC Bank's Part-Time Chairman
articles.nri_angle: HDFC Bank is the most widely held Indian stock among NRI investors — the new chairman's track record of cleaning up banking governance directly affects the governance premium that overseas shareholders pay for India's largest private lender.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank's CEO Just Said He Won't Stay — and the Stock Dropped 3.3% as a Succession Battle Begins
articles.excerpt: Ashok Vaswani, who took over from founder Uday Kotak just three years ago, informed the board he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in December 2026 — leaving India's fourth-largest private bank searching for its third CEO in four years.
articles.image_caption: A Kotak Mahindra Bank branch, one of the most widely held Indian banking stocks among NRI investors
articles.nri_angle: Kotak Mahindra Bank is one of the most widely held Indian stocks among NRI investors — the CEO transition and valuation correction raise key portfolio questions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
